req.title: /status/<code> accepts POST
req.statement: The system shall accept POST requests on /status/<code> and return the requested code.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /status/<code> must return the requested HTTP status code. I design tests covering: (1) a standard 2xx positive case (200), (2) a negative/client-error case (400), (3) boundary cases at the edges of common status code ranges (100, 299, 300, 500), (4) an invalid code negative path, and (5) a 5xx server-error code. Each test uses exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator and constant mutations. The view_status_code handler in core.py accepts POST via the methods list ['GET','POST','PUT','DELETE','PATCH','TRACE'], and delegates to the status_code() helper in helpers.py which sets r.status_code = code exactly.
